nations.name: Native Village of Eklutna
nations.lands: Alaska; the Tribal government describes community work in Eklutna Village and Anchorage

facts.text: The Tribe dates the organization of its government office to 1961, describing protection of land rights as its purpose. This is an office milestone, not the beginning of its self-government.
The Tribe describes its government as traditional rather than formed under the Indian Reorganization Act, with seven Council members serving staggered three-year terms.
facts.evidence: Seven (7) Council Members serve three (3) year staggered terms.

facts.text: The Tribe describes using National Historic Preservation Act Section 106 and other legislation to mitigate impacts on traditional resources and support inclusion of Dena’ina history on public signage.
facts.evidence: utilize NHPA (National Historic Preservation Act) Section 106

facts.text: The Tribe reports working with partners on assessment, planning and restoration of the Eklutna River. The page describes ongoing work, not a completed restoration.
facts.evidence: assessment, planning, and restoration of the Eklutna River.
